why: The repair is independent of the disputed oil number: XLV reclaimed its 50D ($166.75) on Monday, before the Fed said a word, and never surrendered it, voiding the prior week's trap call (wiki/healthcare.md Catalyst 1; wiki/synthesis.md Section 2). This is the one confirmation in the healthcare file that does not route through 'oil broke'.

The oversold-spring trade paid on schedule -- TMO +6.9 pct to a new 52-week high, ISRG +6.6 pct, DHR +5.8 pct, GILD +5.0 pct (wiki/healthcare.md Catalyst 3) -- and the sector's SPY correlation is only 0.324 (wiki/canary-watch.md SECTOR CORRELATION MATRIX), so it is still supplying diversification in a week when seven of twelve sectors were in outflow.

Discount applied: the desk's Catalyst 2 attributes the +1.8 pct week to 'oil collapsed -4.6 pct to $95.47', which does not reproduce (wiki/synthesis.md Contradiction 1). regime_fit 62 rather than matching the 80/90/80.9 arithmetic is that discount.
risks: Earnings density is Low -- nothing reports until UNH/JNJ on Oct 13 (wiki/earnings-surveillance.md) -- so the week has no sector-specific catalyst and trades purely on rates.
DXY +1.11 pct is a flagged Q3 translation drag on big pharma (wiki/synthesis.md Wire 5); falsifier is a close under $164-165.

why: The month column says the damage is not repaired -- -3.19 pct vs SPY on the month, breadth 20 of 100 and volume confirmation 16.5 of 100 -- so the week was a mean-reversion bounce off a trial-failure week, not a trend (wiki/canary-watch.md SECTOR ROTATION FLOW; staged metrics).

Healthcare's correlation has risen for two straight weeks (0.250 -> 0.324) after a sign flip (wiki/canary-watch.md SECTOR CORRELATION MATRIX), which erodes exactly the defensive property the week's score rests on.
risks: XBI lost its 50D ($157.57) again on Friday and needs a weekly close above $158-160 to restore the truce (wiki/synthesis.md Section 5); LLY at all-time highs is a hold, not an add.
Q3 prints land Oct 13-14, at the far edge of the window (wiki/earnings-surveillance.md).

extracts.lead_summary: The fortress took the Fed's first hike in three years and did not yield an inch: XLV +1.8% to $168.39, the 50-day reclaimed on Monday and defended all week, while the bombs of two weeks ago reversed — AMGN +2.2% off the Lp(a) wreck, SYK flat at its low, and the oversold medtech pile (TMO +6.9%, ISRG +6.6%, DHR +5.8%) produced the sector's best snapback of the year. Eli Lilly printed new all-time highs above $1T again. The week's two honest wounds: CVS -6.2% on no headline, and an XBI that +0.3%'d — alive, but still under its 50-day while IOVA +19% and SDGR +52% proved the event money never left biotech, it just got pickier.
